items.title: Banwa : le Conseil Provincial de Secours d’Urgence et de Réhabilitation distribue des vivres à 3500 ménages à Solenzo
items.description: Banwa : le Conseil Provincial de Secours d'Urgence et de Réhabilitation distribue des vivres à 3500 ménages à Solenzo Solenzo, 3 août 2026 (AIB) – Le président du Conseil Provincial de Secours d'Urgence et de Réhabilitation (COPROSUR) Sanfiénalé Joseph Sirima, Haut-Commissaire de la province des Banwa a procédé le lundi 3 août 2026, au lancement de la distribution gratuite de vivres au profit de 3500 ménages dans la cour de la direction provinciale de la famille et de la solidarité nationale. Le COPROSUR a procédé à la distribution gratuite de 98,1 tonnes de riz de 25 kg, de 70 tonnes de farine de maïs de 20 kg, de 40 tonnes de semoule de maïs de 25 kg, de 150 cartons de pâte alimentaire, de 100 litres d'huile et de 10 sacs de sel de 25 kg aux personnes retournées, aux PDI sur place à Solenzo et aux hôtes vulnérables de la commune de Solenzo. Chaque ménage va bénéficier au cours de cette distribution gratuite de 2 sacs de spéculations différentes (un sac de riz de 25 kg et un sac de farine de maïs de 20 kg ou un sac de riz de 25 kg et un sac de semoule de maïs de 25 kg), de 2,5 litres d'huile, de 4 paquets de spaghetti et d'un kilogramme de sel. Le Haut-Commissaire a rappelé aux bénéficiaires l'interdiction de la vente des vivres reçus au marché. Mariatou Séré se dit très fière de recevoir ce don. « Je n'ai pas de mari ni d’enfant qui s'occupe de moi. Avec ce sac de riz et de farine, je ne vais plus mourir de faim » a-t-elle affirmé au micro de l'AIB. Agence d'Information du Burkina SO/wis

items.title: Burkina : Les députés adoptent la loi portant création de l’ARCOD, issue de la fusion du CSC et de la CIL
items.description: BURKINA-COMMUNICATION-DONNEES-LEGISLATION Burkina : Les députés adoptent la loi portant création de l'ARCOD, issue de la fusion du CSC et de la CIL Ouagadougou, 4 août 2026 (AIB)-Les députés de l'Assemblée législative du Peuple (ALP) ont adopté hier lundi le projet de loi portant organisation de l' Autorité de régulation de la communication et des données (ARCOD), issu de la fusion du Conseil supérieur de la Communication (CSC) et de la Commission de l’informatique et des libertés (CIL). Examiné en séance plénière sous la présidence du président de l'Assemblée législative du Peuple, Dr Ousmane Bougouma, le texte a été défendu par le ministre de la Justice et des Droits humains, chargé des Relations avec les institutions, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala. L'ARCOD est issue de la fusion du Conseil supérieur de la communication (CSC), organe de régulation des médias créé en 1995, et de la Commission de l'informatique et des libertés (CIL), autorité chargée de la protection des données personnelles instituée en 2004 et opérationnelle depuis 2007. Cette réorganisation répond à la convergence progressive des missions des deux institutions, portées par la montée en puissance des technologies numériques, qui les amenait à intervenir sur des terrains proches, notamment la protection de la vie privée, la gestion des données personnelles et la surveillance des contenus en ligne. Le ministre Bayala a précisé que la création de l'ARCOD permet désormais de rassembler deux missions jusqu'alors séparées : la régulation de la communication publique, héritée du CSC, et la supervision du traitement des données personnelles, auparavant confiée à la CIL. Cette fusion s'inscrit dans le cadre des dispositions de la Constitution révisée du 20 janvier 2026. La réforme vise à doter le Burkina Faso d'une autorité unique chargée de réguler le secteur de la communication et de veiller au respect des règles relatives à la protection des données à caractère personnel, dans un contexte marqué par l'essor rapide des technologies numériques. Le projet de loi intervient dans le prolongement de l'adoption de la nouvelle législation sur la protection des données à caractère personnel. Il fixe notamment les missions, les attributions, l'organisation, la composition et les modalités de fonctionnement de l'ARCOD. Le texte accorde également à l'autorité un pouvoir réglementaire devant lui permettre d'adapter son action aux évolutions technologiques et aux nouveaux usages numériques. Au cours des débats, les députés ont formulé des observations sur plusieurs aspects du projet de loi, notamment la composition du collège de l'autorité, les modalités de renouvellement des mandats de ses membres et certaines dispositions transitoires. En réponse, le ministre Edasso Rodrigue Bayala a expliqué que le renouvellement échelonné des membres du premier collège permettra de préserver la mémoire institutionnelle et d'assurer la continuité de l'action de l'autorité. Il a également indiqué que le pouvoir réglementaire reconnu à l'ARCOD devrait lui permettre d'encadrer plus efficacement les évolutions technologiques, notamment dans le domaine de l'intelligence artificielle, en complément des mesures réglementaires que le Gouvernement pourrait prendre. L'adoption de cette loi doit ainsi permettre au Burkina Faso de renforcer son dispositif institutionnel en matière de régulation de la communication et de protection des données à caractère personnel, alors que les usages numériques connaissent une évolution rapide. Agence d’information du Burkina ATA/as Source : ALP

items.title: Quand la Haute-Volta est devenue Burkina Faso
items.description: En modifiant le nom de son pays un an après la révolution du 4 août 1983, le capitaine Thomas Sankara n'a pas seulement réécrit la carte de l'Afrique de l'Ouest. Il a posé la première pierre d'un projet de société panafricain fondé sur la souveraineté, l'honneur et l'autosuffisance. Le 4 août est une date profondément gravée dans la mémoire collective continentale. Il y a 42 ans, en 1984, les autorités voltaïques opéraient une rupture symbolique décisive avec le passé colonial en rebaptisant la Haute-Volta. Depuis lors, le pays est appelé «Burkina Faso», une fusion des langues mooré et dioula pour signifier «la patrie des hommes intègres». Proclamée lors du premier anniversaire du coup d'État révolutionnaire qui a porté Thomas Sankara au pouvoir à l'âge de 33 ans, cette refonte identitaire ne s'est pas arrêtée aux cartes géographiques. Elle s'est accompagnée de la naissance d'un nouveau drapeau, de la composition d'un hymne national inédit et du choix de nouveaux symboles républicains. L'objectif était clair: forger une conscience nationale renouvelée, affranchie des tares du colonialisme et tournée vers la justice sociale. Durant son passage au pouvoir, le jeune dirigeant a impulsé des transformations radicales dans tous les secteurs: Autonomie économique et agricole: une quête prioritaire d'autosuffisance alimentaire pour affranchir le peuple de la dépendance extérieure. Progrès social et égalité: un engagement pionnier pour la promotion des droits des femmes et la protection de la nature. Gouvernance exemplaire: une lutte intransigeante contre la corruption et une affirmation ferme de la souveraineté nationale face aux ingérences étrangères. Si l'expérience révolutionnaire s'est tragiquement interrompue lors de l'assassinat de Thomas Sankara le 15 octobre 1987, l'impact de ces réformes n'a jamais faibli. Plus de trois décennies après sa disparition, la figure de Sankara et les idéaux du 4 août demeurent une source d'inspiration inépuisable. Dans un continent en quête permanente de repères, l'histoire du «pays des hommes intègres» continue de résonner comme un appel vibrant à la dignité, au panafricanisme et à la réappropriation par les Africains de leur propre destin. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Quand la Haute-Volta est devenue Burkina Faso est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: La JSK choisit la Tunisie pour son stage d’intersaison
items.description: La JS Kabylie poursuit sa préparation d’intersaison en Tunisie. Le club le plus titré d’Algérie a posé ses valises dans la ville d’Aïn Draham pour 12 jours de préparation. Sous la conduite de son nouvel entraîneur, le Franco-Algérien Karim Belhocine, et avec ses nouvelles recrues estivales, la JSK va disputer plusieurs rencontres en Tunisie. « Les Jaune et Vert séjourneront à l'hôtel La Forêt, où ils poursuivront leur préparation dans un environnement propice au travail et à la récupération », a annoncé ce mardi dans un communiqué la direction du club propriété de l’opérateur de téléphonie mobile Mobilis qui court derrière un titre de champion d’Algérie depuis 2008. « Ce regroupement sera rythmé par plusieurs rencontres amicales, qui permettront au staff technique de poursuivre le travail entrepris depuis la reprise, d'affiner les automatismes et d'évaluer la progression du groupe avant l'entame de la nouvelle saison », a indiqué la direction de la JSK dans le communiqué. JSK : Belaid et Hadid quittent le club La JSK, qui a entamé la préparation de la saison 2026-2027 le 6 juillet dernier au stade Hocine Ait Ahmed de Tizi-Ouzou, a enregistré le départ de plusieurs joueurs dont le deuxième gardien Hadid vers l’USMA, Hamza Mouali vers Akbou et le défenseur central Zinedine Belaid qui a rejoint le club saoudien d’𝗔𝗹 𝗧𝗮𝗮𝘄𝗼𝘂𝗻 pour trois saisons. Le montant de transfert de l’international algérien est de 1,2 million d’euros. Pour les arrivées, le club a annoncé le recrutement d’autres joueurs dont le défenseur central mauritanien Nouh Mohamed El Abd et l’attaquant Abdennour-Iheb Belhocini. items.title: Casablanca relance le projet d'une grande salle omnisports à Aïn Sebaâ
items.description: Le projet de construction d'une grande salle omnisports à Aïn Sebaâ est de nouveau d'actualité. Après plusieurs années de retard, les autorités relancent ce chantier stratégique, appelé à renforcer les infrastructures sportives et événementielles de Casablanca à l'approche des grandes échéances internationales, dont la CAN 2027 et la Coupe du monde 2030. Prévue sur une superficie d'environ 50.000 m², cette salle couverte multidisciplinaire s'inscrit parmi les projets structurants destinés à transformer le littoral est de la métropole. Bien qu'approuvé par le Conseil communal en 2023, le projet avait été retardé en raison de difficultés liées au foncier et au financement. Conçue selon les standards internationaux, la future enceinte pourra accueillir de nombreuses disciplines sportives en salle, notamment le basket-ball, le handball, le volley-ball, les sports de combat ou encore la gymnastique. Elle répondra également aux exigences nécessaires pour l'organisation de compétitions continentales et internationales. Au-delà de sa vocation sportive, l'infrastructure sera polyvalente. Elle pourra recevoir des concerts, des congrès, des salons professionnels, des expositions et d'autres manifestations culturelles, artistiques ou économiques, renforçant ainsi l'offre événementielle de Casablanca. La concrétisation du projet passera par une procédure d'expropriation pour cause d'utilité publique concernant deux parcelles situées sur le front de mer. Les travaux comprendront également l'aménagement des accès, le raccordement aux différents réseaux ainsi que la réorganisation des espaces environnants afin de faciliter l'accès au site. Cette nouvelle salle s'inscrit dans un vaste programme de requalification du littoral d'Aïn Sebaâ et de Sidi Bernoussi. Les autorités souhaitent faire de cette façade maritime un pôle dédié au sport, aux loisirs, à la culture et au tourisme, tout en améliorant le cadre de vie des habitants. Le projet figure aussi parmi les principales réalisations prévues par le nouveau plan d'aménagement de Casablanca, qui prévoit la création de nouveaux espaces verts, de pistes cyclables et piétonnes ainsi que d'équipements sportifs destinés aux quartiers de l'est de la ville. Sa relance intervient enfin dans un contexte de modernisation accélérée des infrastructures marocaines, en prévision des grands rendez-vous sportifs que le Royaume accueillera dans les prochaines années, avec pour ambition de doter Casablanca d'un équipement multifonctionnel répondant aux standards internationaux. The post Casablanca relance le projet d'une grande salle omnisports à Aïn Sebaâ appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: BBNaija: ‘Don’t make us most boring set’ — Sheba fumes at housemates
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab BBNaija Season 11 Head of House (HoH), Sheba, has issued a stern warning to her fellow housemates, expressing frustration over what she described as their lack of commitment during preparations for this week’s wager presentation. An irritated Sheba, while speaking during a rehearsal on Tuesday morning, fumed at housemates to take the task seriously, insisting that everyone had a responsibility to contribute to the team’s success. “If you want to play a game, you have to step up or step away. I will not run mad. We are not kids,” she said. Reminding the contestants why they signed up for the reality show, Sheba stressed that the Big Brother house is first and foremost an entertainment platform. “You came to an entertainment show. Whether you are a lawyer, doctor, teacher or professor, this is an entertainment show and you have to entertain,” she said. Sheba added that every housemate must find a way to contribute, regardless of their strengths. “If you cannot act, you will sing. If you will not sing, just find yourself. You just have to find a place and put yourself in this wager,” she said. Sheba also warned against allowing poor participation to define the Season 11 cast. “You are not going to put the team or the house down. You are not going to make us be said that we are the most boring set that Big Brother has ever had,” she declared. According to the Head of House, every contestant earned a place in the competition because of the energy they displayed during auditions and should continue to live up to that standard. “You put yourself here because of your energy. If you did not show them big energy, I promise you, you will not be here,” she said. Sheba concluded by urging the housemates to respect the rules of the game, warning that she would not hesitate to speak to them more firmly if they continued to take the task lightly. “If you want me to respect you, you have to respect Big Brother’s house and Big Brother’s rules or I promise you I will talk to you like kids. This is becoming ridiculous,” she said. The outburst comes as housemates intensify preparations for their first wager presentation under Sheba’s leadership, with the Head of House pushing for a performance that will impress Big Brother and avoid a failed wager. items.title: Financement du développement : le Maroc dans le Top 10 mondial des pays attirant le plus de capitaux privés
items.description: Le Maroc figure parmi les dix principaux bénéficiaires mondiaux des capitaux privés mobilisés grâce aux interventions publiques de développement. Selon le Private Finance Mobilisation Report 2026 de l'OCDE, le Royaume a attiré en moyenne 1,5 milliard de dollars par an entre 2021 et 2024, confirmant son statut de destination privilégiée pour les investisseurs internationaux dans les économies émergentes. Le Maroc continue de renforcer son attractivité auprès des investisseurs internationaux. Dans son rapport 2026 consacré à la mobilisation des financements privés, l'Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques (OCDE) classe le Royaume parmi les dix premiers bénéficiaires mondiaux des capitaux privés mobilisés par les institutions publiques de développement. Avec une moyenne annuelle de 1,5 milliard de dollars de financements privés mobilisés entre 2021 et 2024, le Maroc occupe la 10ᵉ place mondiale ex aequo, aux côtés d'autres économies émergentes particulièrement dynamiques. Il s'agit d'un indicateur distinct des flux traditionnels d'investissements directs étrangers (IDE) : il mesure les capitaux privés que les banques multilatérales de développement, les agences de coopération ou les institutions financières publiques parviennent à attirer vers des projets grâce à des mécanismes de partage des risques, de garanties ou de financement mixte. Le rapport souligne que seuls le Brésil et l'Inde devancent nettement les autres pays bénéficiaires, suivis notamment par le Mozambique, la Turquie, le Maroc et le Mexique. À eux seuls, le Brésil et l'Inde concentrent près d'un quart des financements privés mobilisés au niveau mondial sur la période étudiée. Le Maroc profite de la montée en puissance de l'Afrique Cette performance s'inscrit dans une dynamique continentale favorable. L'Afrique est devenue la première région bénéficiaire des financements privés mobilisés, captant 30 % du total mondial, soit près de 19,7 milliards de dollars par an entre 2021 et 2024. Les garanties, les investissements directs dans les entreprises et les prêts syndiqués constituent les principaux instruments utilisés pour attirer ces capitaux vers le continent. Pour l'OCDE, cette concentration des financements sur l'Afrique traduit un intérêt croissant des investisseurs pour des marchés offrant un potentiel de croissance élevé, dès lors que les risques sont partiellement couverts par les institutions de développement. Le rapport rappelle toutefois que ces financements demeurent fortement concentrés sur les pays à revenu intermédiaire. Ceux-ci ont capté près de 69 % des montants mobilisés entre 2021 et 2024, tandis que les pays les moins avancés n'en ont reçu que 8 %. Cette répartition reflète les différences de profondeur des marchés financiers, de stabilité macroéconomique et de perception du risque par les investisseurs privés. Des financements orientés vers les secteurs les plus bancables À l'échelle mondiale, les capitaux privés mobilisés se dirigent principalement vers les secteurs offrant les modèles économiques les plus solides. Les infrastructures économiques et les services concentrent près de 70 % des financements, devant les activités industrielles, minières et agricoles. À l'inverse, les secteurs sociaux, tels que la santé ou l'éducation, restent nettement moins attractifs pour les investisseurs privés en raison de modèles de rentabilité plus limités. L'OCDE observe également qu'environ 40 % des financements privés mobilisés soutiennent des projets liés à l'action climatique. La majorité est orientée vers les projets de réduction des émissions de gaz à effet de serre, tandis que les investissements consacrés à l'adaptation aux effets du changement climatique demeurent beaucoup plus modestes. Au niveau mondial, les interventions publiques de développement ont permis de mobiliser plus de 600 milliards de dollars de capitaux privés entre 2012 et 2024, avec un record annuel de 77 milliards de dollars atteint en 2024. Malgré cette progression, l'OCDE estime que les volumes restent insuffisants face aux besoins de financement liés aux Objectifs de développement durable et à la transition climatique, appelant à un recours accru aux garanties, au financement mixte et aux autres mécanismes de partage des risques afin d'attirer davantage d'investisseurs privés. Au rythme du Stambali | Un moment de solidarité et de résistance avec Saadia Mosbah
items.description: Amnesty International Tunisie nous fait parvenir le texte dont la traduction est publiée ci-dessous dans le cadre de la «Mobilisation de solidarité avec Saadia Mosbah, militante des droits humains et présidente de l'association Mnemty, actuellement emprisonnée en Tunisie en raison de son engagement pour la défense des droits des personnes noires et la lutte contre le racisme.» Nous prenons la parole aujourd’hui — alors qu’elle reste privée de liberté, suscitant de vives inquiétudes quant à son intégrité physique ainsi qu’à l’exercice de ses droits aux soins, aux visites et à la communication — pour affirmer que la défense de l’égalité et de la justice ne saurait justifier ni sanction ni isolement. C’est un appel à la solidarité avec elle, ainsi qu’à assumer une responsabilité collective face au racisme et pour la préservation de la dignité de toute personne vivant en Tunisie. Dans le Stambali, les sonorités du «gumbri» et des «chaqchaq» se mêlent aux corps au fil de la «nouba» . C’est un art qui porte en lui la mémoire de l’esclavage, du déracinement et du racisme, mais qui véhicule aussi un autre message : celui de ne jamais laisser seul celui que les épreuves et l’injustice ont accablé. Dans l’histoire de la résistance à l’esclavage, à la ségrégation et à la discrimination, les femmes noires n’ont pas été de simples figures accrochées aux murs de la mémoire une fois les combats achevés. Elles en ont été le cœur battant, rassemblant ce que la peur avait dispersé : voix, droits et liens humains. Des champs de coton et des convois d’esclaves a émergé une mémoire refusant de réduire la violence à un passé révolu, transformant la marginalisation et l’isolement qu’elle a engendrés en une conscience commune de la résistance et du droit à la justice. C’est à travers cet héritage que nous te comprenons, Saadia : non pas comme une femme dont le corps seul porterait le poids d’une cause entière, mais comme une part d’une mémoire collective ayant su transformer une expérience partagée en une conscience politique qui met au jour les mécanismes de l’exclusion. La lutte pour la visibilité, l’appartenance et la pleine citoyenneté est devenue une exigence générale, plaçant l’État et la société face à leurs responsabilités dans le combat contre le racisme, au-delà de la simple condamnation de certaines de ses manifestations. Tu as levé le voile sur le mur du déni entourant le racisme, démontrant que ce qui est présenté comme un détail anodin cesse de l’être dès lors qu’il se répète et s’ancre dans le quotidien des gens. Ces petits signes s’accumulent pour ériger des frontières invisibles : entre ceux à qui l’on accorde d’emblée sa confiance et ceux que l’on accueille avec méfiance ; entre ceux qui traversent l’espace public sans avoir à se justifier et ceux à qui l’on rappelle, sans relâche, que leur appartenance même est remise en question. Ainsi, tes propos sur les Tunisiennes et les Tunisiens noirs portaient sur la Tunisie elle-même : sur une histoire que le pays tend à raconter en gommant ses fissures, et sur un présent où le discours sur la diversité ne suffit pas tant qu’il ne se traduit pas en réalité. Tu n’as pas réclamé une place en marge du récit national ; tu as plutôt souligné que ce récit demeure incomplet tant que ceux qui en ont longtemps été tenus à l’écart en restent absents. Car la reconnaissance ne s’accomplit pas dans les discours, mais se manifeste dans le monde du travail, à l’école et dans les administrations, ainsi que dans le droit de chacun à traverser la rue sans que son corps ne suscite la méfiance ou qu’il ne soit contraint de justifier son humanité. Tu as dit ce qui devait être dit et tu as enduré, pour cela, un fardeau qu’aucune personne ne devrait avoir à porter seule. Aujourd’hui, ta sécurité ainsi que tes droits aux soins, aux visites et à la communication ne sont pas des détails accessoires ; ce sont des droits fondamentaux qui touchent à ta liberté et à ta dignité. Ton emprisonnement ne constitue pas seulement une privation arbitraire de liberté, mais une attaque politique visant ton action en faveur des droits humains et ta lutte contre la discrimination systémique ; c’est la punition d’une femme qui a refusé la marginalisation, ainsi qu’une tentative de réduire au silence une voix ayant mis en lumière les failles du système et d’intimider quiconque choisit de briser le mur du déni pour lutter contre le racisme. Se tenir à tes côtés signifie ne pas laisser la prison rompre les liens qui t’unissent à ceux qui t’aiment et se soucient de toi. Tu es une femme qui connaît la fatigue, la peur et le besoin de sécurité ; une mère, une amie et une compagne qui a tant donné aux autres. Les paroles que tu as prononcées et les questions que tu as soulevées concernant la justice et le racisme ne doivent pas peser sur tes seules épaules ; elles constituent une responsabilité que nous partageons tous. Lors des cérémonies de Stambali, la souffrance n’est jamais laissée seule face à celui ou celle qui l’éprouve ; le rythme, le souffle et la présence des autres l’enveloppent jusqu’à ce qu'elle trouve une autre voie vers la guérison. C’est ainsi que nous te voulons parmi nous : proche de nous telle que tu es, mère, amie et compagne chère. Le fardeau que tu as porté pour la lutte des personnes noires en Tunisie est une responsabilité partagée, et non une facture qui te serait laissée à régler seule. Amnesty International Tunisie Traduit de l'arabe. L’article Au rythme du Stambali | Un moment de solidarité et de résistance avec Saadia Mosbah est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: AJK elections: Voting concludes in two constituencies as PPP again alleges rigging
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Voting in two AJK constituencies concluded on Tuesday after it could not be held on the scheduled date of Aug 2 during the second phase of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir elections, as the PPP again alleged rigging. Authorities had postponed polling in LA-27 Muzaffarabad-I (Kutla) and at 71 of the 174 polling stations in LA-28 Muzaffarabad-II (Lachhrat) due to landslides and bad weather, which had resulted in blocked roads. Elections in AJK are being held in three phases due to security concerns, with polling having been held on seven seats of Muzaffarabad division and 12 refugee seats — reserved seats for refugees from India-occupied Kashmir — on Sunday. In the third phase, elections will be held in 11 constituencies of Poonch division on August 10. The first phase of polling was held in AJK’s Mirpur division on July 27, in which the PML-N had secured nine of the 13 seats while the PPP won the remaining four. The two parties, which are allies in Centre, have been engaged in a war of words since, with the PPP accusing the PML-N of rigging, violence and electoral malpractices. Rigging allegations It levelled the same allegations on Tuesday, with the party posting a complaint on its X account that it said it had sent to the Election Commission. It claimed that polling staff had been “caught red-handed with official ballot papers and polling bags inside the house of a PML-N supporter, approximately two kilometres from the designated polling site” in LA-27 Muzaffarabad-I (Kotla) in union council Bheri. The PPP claimed it had “concrete evidence” that polling staff at polling station no.3 had moved to the residence of a PML-N candidate and abandoned their post. It also shared a statement by PPP Vice President Sherry Rehman on X, with her saying that and the reports of the presence of polling staff at a PML-N supporter’s residence were concerning. She said videos related to “rigging by the PML-N” had been handed over to the Election Commission as evidence and demanded immediate disciplinary and legal action. When Dawn asked Election Commission official Khawaja Muhammed Ahsan about the videos, he said a PPP worker had shared some videos, but “they are vague and amount to a little more than unverified allegations”. “Unless the footage is authenticated through proper forensic examination and corroborated by other credible evidence, it cannot be treated as proof,” he added. Meanwhile, the PPP shared another complaint addressed to the Election Commission on X. It accused the PML-N of ballot stuffing at polling stations no.95 and no.97 in LA-28 and of obstructing the polling process by barring voters from casting their votes. The PPP also alleged that at polling station no.92 in LA-27, the presiding officer was stuffing ballots and called for him to be replaced by someone “neutral”. In yet another complaint, the PPP accused PML-N workers of firing in Bandi in LA-28 to “terrorise the residents of Bandi and keep them inside their homes so that they do not proceed to the polling stations”. Tallal Chaudhry tells Bilawal to ’show grace in defeat’ Meanwhile, Minister of State for Interior and PML-N’s election coordinator for Poonch division, Tallal Chaudhry, rejected earlier allegations of rigging made by PPP in the AJK elections and took a swipe at PPP chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, saying “leaders should not cry over defeat”, according to a statement issued by the interior ministry. Presiding over a review meeting on the third phase of AJK elections in Poonch division, Chaudhry said PML-N’s sweeping victory in the first two phases was a reflection of public trust in the performance of the federal and Punjab governments. “The people of Kashmir have voted for work and performance,” he told district constituency coordinators and PML-N candidates from Poonch division who attended the meeting. Seemingly responding to PPP’s allegations related to electoral malpractices, the minister said: “Bilawal Bhutto should show a big heart. Leaders do not look good when they cry over defeat.” He added that the mandate given to PML-N in AJK showed that “every part of Pakistan wants to become like Punjab” in terms of development and governance. He expressed confidence that the PML-N would secure a majority of seats in the third phase of the AJK elections. A day earlier, Bilawal had warned the PML-N that a “countdown” for it had begun and declared that his party’s “movement” for people’s rights would extend to the entire country. In a series of clips posted on X on Monday, Bilawal affirmed that his party’s struggle for the people’s right to governance, ownership and employment will continue. The PPP chairman said, “And my message for the friends in PML-N is just this: you can hear that voice, listen carefully, tick tock, tick tock. Your countdown has begun.” Bilawal had given a similar warning last week to the federal government, which is led by the PML-N in alliance with his own PPP. Senior leaders of his party have made similar remarks in recent days, even alleging the PML-N of rigging in the 2024 general elections, which resulted in both parties being part of the current ruling coalition in the Centre. Both parties have also traded barbs over governance, political mandate and provincial performance .

items.title: The Catholic Church’s New Schism
items.description: At an open-air Mass in Écône, Switzerland, before a crowd of about 16,000 people, four priests became bishops last month. The men professed their fidelity to tradition against “heretics, schismatics, and those who rebel against our Holy Father.” They did so knowing full well that, in becoming bishops, they lacked something the Catholic Church deems essential: permission from the pope. All four of these men are members of the Society of Saint Pius X, or SSPX, an arch-traditionalist group of clergy founded in 1970 by the French archbishop Marcel Lefebvre. For decades, SSPX has battled with the Vatican over the group’s fear that, as one theologian told me, “in reading the signs of the times, the Catholic Church is more beholden to the times than she is a light to the nations.” Now tensions have reached a breaking point. The Vatican warned SSPX before the Écône Mass that consecrating bishops without a papal mandate would be considered a “schismatic act,” a formal separation from the Catholic Church. After the Mass, the Church issued a decree saying that the new bishops, plus the two who ordained them, incurred an automatic excommunication: They can neither receive communion nor celebrate licit Masses nor officiate valid marriages and confessions. The 700 or so SSPX priests worldwide will also fall into schism, and thereby be excommunicated, if they remain with the society. Even lay churchgoers who “formally adhere” to the group may face the same sanction. [ Read: The real religious ‘renewal’ happening in Gen Z ] By some estimates , 25,000 people in the United States are affiliated with SSPX—a tiny fraction of the roughly 53 million American Catholic adults. Many Catholics may not even know that the Church finds itself in arguably its largest schism since the 19th century. Nonetheless, the SSPX excommunications touch on broader disputes in Catholicism today: about reform, orthodoxy, and whether the Church’s institutional changes of the past half century have been for the better. That is, this schism is about more than just SSPX. It’s also about how the Church will respond to a larger group of traditionalists—those who, though still Catholic, have questioned or even attacked many of the beliefs and practices that characterize the faith today. SSPX’s fight with the Catholic Church began as a response to the Second Vatican Council, or Vatican II, the most pivotal event of 20th-century Catholic history. From 1962 to 1965, the Church instituted a series of reforms that reimagined its role in a secular age. Perhaps most famous was the council’s overhaul of the Mass in hopes of increasing participation among the faithful . In most Masses, priests stopped facing the altar and began facing the people. The local language replaced Latin as the main tongue of worship. In some parishes, out went Gregorian chants and in came guitars. Vatican II also reformed the doctrine of extra ecclesiam nulla salus , or “outside the Church, there is no salvation.” As Larry Chapp, a former theology professor at DeSales University, told me, the council clarified that Catholics “have to be open to the movement of grace outside of the boundaries of the Church.” Guided by this vision, Vatican II produced writings that promoted religious freedom , ecumenical efforts with other Christians, and “dialogue and collaboration” with non-Christian religions. To SSPX, these changes were calamitous. The society’s 28-page profession of faith asserts that true Catholicism rejects ecumenical and interfaith dialogue, and states that other faiths are “false religions” and “the work of the devil.” SSPX also holds fast to the pre–Vatican II Traditional Latin Mass as the only legitimate liturgy: The profession of faith declares that the vernacular Mass “favours heresy, weakens the faith,” and “turns the faithful away from the adoration due to God.” Lefebvre participated in Vatican II himself—he even signed all of the writings that SSPX now objects to. But he soon started denouncing the council’s reforms. Five years after the council concluded, he founded SSPX with the mission of training priests in preconciliar beliefs and practices. In 1974, Lefebvre condemned Vatican II for contributing to “the destruction of the Church,” one of the many accusations and acts of defiance that prompted Church authorities to revoke his permission to run the society. Lefebvre kept recruiting priests anyway. By 1988, SSPX had approximately 200 clergy worldwide, mainly in France, Switzerland, and the United States. In June of that year, Lefebvre ordained four priests as bishops, ignoring Pope John Paul II’s orders not to. The pontiff excommunicated Lefebvre and the four bishops but declared no formal schism. Lefebvre, for his part, continued leading the society—and vehemently opposing Vatican II, which he described as the “adulterous marriage of the Church with liberal ideas”—until his death in 1991. [ Read: The first Millennial saint ] The Vatican let SSPX exist in a kind of limbo state in the years after the 1988 excommunications. Members of the society were officially limited in the sacraments that they could officiate, but SSPX kept ordaining priests and holding illicit Masses. And yet they were still, technically, a part of the Catholic Church. Church leaders, Chapp said, made “efforts to bring them back into the fold.” In 2009, Pope Benedict XVI lifted the excommunications of the four living SSPX bishops that John Paul II had effected two decades prior. A few years later, Pope Francis granted SSPX priests permission to hear confessions and officiate marriages. Still, SSPX has no interest in being part of a Church that doesn’t spurn Vatican II. The society holds that the council’s reforms create a “state of necessity” that allows it to do what it must “to preserve the faith.” This is the irony at the heart of SSPX’s theology: The society claims to be a bulwark of the Catholic faith; it also dismisses the pope’s authority as the final interpreter of that faith. “This is not a trivial issue,” Chapp said. “Staying in union with the vicar of Christ is a central defining feature of what it means to be Catholic.” Although SSPX considers itself a lone defender of tradition, other prominent Catholics—including popes—have expressed concerns about the liturgy and emphasized the importance of doctrinal clarity. Before his pontificate, Pope Benedict XVI worried that Vatican II’s liturgical changes, as implemented, had in some situations downplayed the “authentic inner vibrancy” of the Mass. John Paul II was a consistent proponent of interfaith dialogue, but nonetheless cautioned in 1990 against “a religious relativism which leads to the belief that ‘one religion is as good as another.’” But these popes—and many other Catholics who have raised questions about the implementation of certain Church reforms—were working within the Church, not against it. SSPX, by contrast, “doesn’t have to wrestle with unclarity or ambiguity,” Father Gregory Pine, a professor of moral theology at the Dominican House of Studies in Washington, D.C., told me. It doesn’t do the hard theological work of interpreting new teachings alongside tradition. It simply maintains a posture of rejection—and calls it orthodoxy. It’s one thing for a tiny sect to go rogue. But traditionalism has many supporters in the broader Catholic Church—which means that how the Church moves forward has implications not only for SSPX but also for this larger set of traditionalists, and for the unity of the Church as a whole. Like SSPX, some traditionalists have been viciously critical of the pope, especially during Francis’s pontificate. On a 2024 visit to Singapore, for example, the late pontiff met with an interfaith group of youth and said that “all religions are paths to God”—an off-the-cuff comment that reflected a Vatican II teaching that non-Christian religions “often reflect a ray of that Truth which enlightens all.” Still, several prominent Catholic traditionalists denounced Francis. One said that he spouted “heresy that flies in the face of Jesus Christ.” Another created a video titled “Pope Francis Is a Heretic Denying Tradition, Part 2” that echoed arguments SSPX had made before. The Traditional Latin Mass also has a following beyond SSPX. Roughly 1 million American Catholic adults attend it weekly, which is just 2 percent of the country’s overall Catholic adult population but still many more people than are affiliated with the society. The SSPX excommunications contain a clear message to all traditionalists: Vatican II itself is not up for debate. The council’s teachings and reforms are essential components of the faith, not optional addenda to it. Some Catholics believe that the Church should also continue its official position of limiting access to the Traditional Latin Mass. The Catholic writer Mike Lewis told me that support for the liturgy tends to come with an “entire theological structure” that questions the authority of Vatican II and, by extension, the pope. [ Read: What the fastest-growing Christian group says about America ] Father Pine, however, said that some proponents of the Traditional Latin Mass are simply looking for a liturgy that is “celebrated worthily” and at a “transcendent register.” And some Church leaders have signaled an openness to the Traditional Latin Mass in the weeks since the excommunications. Archbishop Salvatore Cordileone—whom Pope Leo XIV recently appointed to the Vatican’s highest court—has called for “more access” to the liturgy, and some U.S. bishops have promoted it as part of their pleas to SSPX’s followers to return to the Church. Leo XIV has stressed unity since he became pope, last year, and he has not made his position on the Traditional Latin Mass fully known. In excommunicating SSPX, he rebuked a small group of the most vocal supporters of the Traditional Latin Mass. But he has also met with a well-known proponent of the liturgy, as well as with the authors of a forthcoming book that argues that Traditional Latin Mass–goers aren’t the recalcitrants their critics make them out to be. Excommunication, the theologians I spoke with told me, serves a dual purpose: It’s punitive, but it’s also medicinal, meant to call a person or group back to communion. SSPX’s lay members, by early indications , plan to remain in schism for the time being. Those who return, though, may well find their Church to be a bit more open to traditionalism than they imagined it would be.

items.title: One Problem With Attacking the Smithsonian? Americans Like It.
items.description: Earlier this year, I visited a “ Freedom Truck ,” one of the patriotic mobile museums that the Trump administration is sending around the country for the nation’s 250 birthday. There, I had a wide-ranging conversation with a visitor who complained that the U.S. education system is not teaching what she called true history. But when I mentioned the Smithsonian, her disposition changed entirely. She’d heard rumors about “a lot of liberalism going through the Smithsonian now,” she told me, but added, “I love the Smithsonian. I don’t have a problem with it.” I hear this a lot, actually. Even now, as the museum complex continues to face a pressure campaign from the White House, public fondness for the Smithsonian—for its free entry and eclectic collections—is hard to break among those otherwise receptive to President Trump’s anti-institutionalism. Attacks on the credibility of institutions, especially those that disseminate information—universities, public schools, media organizations—have become commonplace in this so-called post-truth age. Recent data from Gallup , published last month, suggested that confidence in the majority of institutions asked about in the survey, including newspapers, public schools, and TV news, is at or near historic lows. Pollsters, meanwhile, don’t even include museums in the Gallup surveys. Although museums have certainly faced some criticism from the left and right, until now, they’ve been largely immune to the most deleterious effects of the culture wars. This may be because most Americans, unlike the president, seem to trust these entities to do their thing. A YouGov survey last week found that 57 percent of Americans said that the amount of influence the president should have over exhibits and programming at federally funded museums should be “none” or “not much.” Just 17 percent of Republicans seemed to take the president’s position: that he should have a “great deal” of influence. Coming after a history museum may not be the base-galvanizing issue the White House hopes it is. Industry data support these findings. In a survey this year, Wilkening Consulting, in partnership with the American Alliance of Museums, found that when people were asked whether museums, faced with pressure, should remove content on topics such as slavery and climate change, the majority of conservatives (63 percent) and liberals (83 percent) disagreed. An oft-cited statistic from the same pair of organizations places museums among the most trusted sources of information in American life, falling just behind public libraries and family and friends. It suggests that museums occupy a rare and cozy place in the collective imagination. At a time of high mistrust in not just institutions but also observable reality, people seem to still find a sense of stability in these keepers of public memory. Perhaps it makes sense that Americans would put their last bits of trust in the very places that show them what is physically, tangibly real. For more than a year, the White House has threatened and criticized the Smithsonian, accusing it of spreading divisive narratives and failing to adequately celebrate American history. In recent weeks, the administration has zeroed in on the National Museum of American History, publishing a lengthy report last month decrying exhibits, calling out staff members, and asserting that the museum has fallen victim to “ideological capture” at the hands of a “radical, activist cohort.” During a pair of congressional hearings , the museum’s director, Anthea Hartig, attested to her love of this country some half a dozen times while maintaining that telling the American story in all of its complexity is a form of respect for its people. Two days later, Trump announced an executive order that would effectively plaster untrustworthy on signs outside the National Museum of American History, like an explicit content label on a CD. The administration ordered the National Park Service to put up the signage in front of the museum to correct what it claims is “inaccurate information” and to share the findings of its report, which claims that the current leadership of the Smithsonian and the history museum cannot be trusted to tell the American story. [ Read: How the Smithsonian could fall ] Right-wing media organizations have echoed this messaging, and since the hearings, Fox News has published dozens of clips and articles criticizing the Smithsonian and scrutinizing its leadership’s pay, highlighting months-old proposed budget cuts, and tallying the number of “liberal items” in a recent exhibit. The Smithsonian, which is partially government-funded , has faced partisan flare-ups over the years. A controversy over how to display the airplane that dropped the atomic bomb over Hiroshima compelled a museum director to resign in 1995. In 2010, Smithsonian leadership removed from the walls of the National Portrait Gallery an artwork showing a crucifix with ants crawling on it after a right-wing outcry. But these incidents involved single exhibits. Now the White House is making a much more comprehensive case against an entire museum and the institution to which it belongs. With the ordered signs, which will direct visitors to Trump-preferred sources of information, the White House is stepping between visitors and historic objects as though to say: Don’t trust what you see inside. Choose us instead. This is where museums and friends and family actually share something in common. Culture wars thrive on the unknown. But museums are an in-person activity. “It’s you directly with that artwork or you directly with that specimen, whatever it is. That object feels like it’s speaking directly to you as a trustworthy thing from the past. That in and of itself lends a lot of credibility,” Susie Wilkening, who runs the American Alliance of Museums’ research about museums and trust, told me. Max van Balgooy, a professor of museum studies at the George Washington University, had similar thoughts: “If you see the gun that John Wilkes Booth used or the chair sat in by John Hancock, you’re sort of faced with the truth,” he told me. “You can’t argue with the real stuff.” Museums weren’t always the hubs of knowledge they are today. They had to both differentiate themselves from the likes of P. T. Barnum’s “museum” as serious scholarly enterprises, devoid of exaggeration and fakes, and invite in ordinary visitors. At the National Museum of History and Technology, which opened in 1964 and went on to become the National Museum of American History, curators strived not just to show objects but also to tell stories, enhanced with well-designed spaces. In the early days, these stories largely celebrated technological progress: When Daniel Boorstin started as the history museum’s director, in 1969, he nodded to the political ruptures of the era and said, “Here, we emphasize the positive. Without denying our failures, we underline and dramatize our successes.” But as more academics joined the museum, they began to stress questions of who, exactly, benefited from American progress, and worked other critical themes into exhibits. The trend—moving from the rah-rah to the sober—was exemplified by a 1987 exhibition that commemorated the bicentennial of the American Constitution and detailed the abuses of Japanese American internment camps. Unlike with other kinds of institutions, such as news sites, naysayers can’t easily form museum alternatives aligned with their perspective. (Partisan museums often struggle to compete with mainstream institutions in terms of historical artifacts.) Part of a museum’s trustworthiness may simply come down to the basic fact that it owns these objects and shows them in an authoritative-looking building. Darryl Hart, a history professor at Hillsdale College, an institution that has worked with the Trump administration on education topics, suggested that museumgoers typically don’t think to critique what they see. “For some people, it’s simply part of what they do on a vacation, and I think they check a box,” he told me. “My sense is, people really are going there fairly innocently, not looking for an agenda.” [ Read: First the Kennedy Center, now the Smithsonian ] The data concur. “On the whole, museums are not believed by the American public to have a political agenda,” Colleen Dilenschneider, the founder of Impacts Experience, a market-research firm that examines perceptions of cultural institutions, told me. Her research, which relies on data from the National Awareness, Attitudes, and Usage Study, found that as of July 1, fewer than a quarter of Americans surveyed believed that museums had political agendas—compared with well over half who believed the same of news sources. Liberals and conservatives both overwhelmingly agreed with the statement that museums are “welcoming to people like me.” Dilenschneider said that “the most shared characteristic of any person in the United States who’s visited a museum in the last year is that they self-identify as a white, non-Hispanic individual” and added that “there are people who are used to hearing their story and they trust that they will continue to hear their story.” Where the story comes from, though, is less clear. Museums contain an essential paradox: They feel transparent because you can walk in and see the work they do. At the same time, the hand behind that work is less visible: As van Balgooy put it, creditless wall texts can read like “the voice of God.” This impersonal feeling is nearly a definitional feature of institutional trust, Oliver Schilke, the director of the Center for Trust Studies at the University of Arizona, told me. “It’s more a trust in a category of things rather than in specific individuals or counterparts,” he said. This slight distance allows us to form an idealized view on an institution. Putting the spotlight on real people behind it can degrade that trust if they’re being attacked or discredited, as happened during the often-acrimonious Smithsonian hearings last month. At times, lawmakers seemed to be speaking directly to their supporters online, such as when Representative Nancy Mace of South Carolina demanded that the history museum’s director tell her whether she believes that men can become women. When Victoria Cain, a professor at Northeastern University who studies the history of museums and education, described museums’ role in life today, she made them sound like a tonic to the most charged parts of contemporary discourse. Akin to secular churches, museums have taken on a ritualistic quality, she told me: “You can go be in a common space with other people in an act of appreciation.” In this regard, museums aren’t just a last bastion of public faith—they’re a rare, shared, bipartisan cultural space. These days, many people lament the ways that we have retreated into information silos, full of others who agree with us. But you can’t chop up Thomas Jefferson’s desk and give half of it to the right and half to the left. If we all want to see the desk where the Declaration of Independence was written, we’re going to have to learn, first, to be in the same room.

items.title: Scrapping Infantino’s World Cup plan was ‘absolutely necessary’ – Wenger
items.description: Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger said the decision to scrap FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s controversial plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup was “absolutely necessary and beyond question”. Wenger works as FIFA’s chief of global football development — he was appointed in 2019 — and the Frenchman became the latest high-profile figure to criticise Infantino’s scheme on Tuesday. Infantino wanted to sell a 20 per cent stake in the World Cup to private equity investors through his FIFA Forward Enterprise. The plan sparked a barrage of criticism for Infantino and has been rejected by three continental confederations, forcing the Italian to ditch his divisive idea. UEFA, European football’s governing body, threatened to boycott the World Cup and other FIFA competitions if Infantino pressed ahead with his plan. Wenger, the most successful manager in Arsenal’s history, joined the chorus of disapproval on Tuesday, making it clear he was opposed to the plan. “The recent events at FIFA deserve some clarity from my side,” he said in a statement. “At FIFA, I am the Chief of Global Football Development. Together with my team, I oversee the data analysis of the game, the FIFA online training centre, the development of youth education through 60 academies across 60 countries where they are most needed, and youth competitions around the world. “In addition, I am a technical adviser to IFAB. I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports. “The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity.” Wenger’s blast followed FIFA’s chief operating officer Kevin Lamour, who said last week that staff at the global governing body had been “deceived” by Infantino. A number of European associations have withdrawn their support for Infantino in a bid to ensure he does not remain in power in the long-term. Infantino is set to stand for re-election in March for a final term as president and would need 106 votes from Fifa’s 211 members to win. The Football Association of Wales (FAW) issued a statement on Monday confirming it had withdrawn its support. The English Football Association are believed to be writing to FIFA to confirm the change in its position. UEFA issued a statement on Saturday welcoming the withdrawal of the FFE plan but stating it had “lost confidence” in Infantino. Clubs within the European Football Clubs group are understood to have contacted FIFA themselves concerned about the scheme. Infantino’s idea was intended to cover Club World Cups and would have affected plans agreed between European clubs and FIFA to create a joint venture on Club World Cup competition rights. items.title: I’m yet to receive reward for Atlanta ’96 triumph – Bonfrère Jo
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Former Nigeria U-23 coach Johannes “Bonfrère” Jo says he is yet to receive any reward or official recognition from the Nigerian government for leading the country’s Dream Team to a historic football gold medal at the 1996 Olympic Games in Atlanta. In a recent interview with The Punch, the Dutch tactician said he remains disappointed that his contribution, 30 years after guiding Nigeria to become the first African nation to win Olympic football gold, has gone largely unacknowledged, despite many members of the victorious squad receiving national honours, houses and cash rewards. “They were claiming that everyone has received their rewards, but I have not received anything; they have never given me the reward for winning the gold medal,” Bonfrère said. He added, “Even my gold medal was stolen from me, and I still didn’t get a reward from the government, which all the players have received, including players who were not on the list.” Bonfrère, now 80, also recounted losing the Olympic gold medal awarded to him after Nigeria’s famous triumph over Argentina in the final, describing the incident as one of the most painful moments of his career. “I don’t know how the medal was collected from me; I only know that when the players went upstairs, an official stopped me from going with them and the medal was gone,” he said. The former coach revealed that he had made repeated attempts to seek recognition from the relevant authorities over the years but had received little response. “I will be happy if something can be done because I have made several calls and sent messages but nobody was interested in helping me,” he said. Bonfrère masterminded one of Nigeria’s greatest sporting achievements at the Atlanta 1996 Olympics, where the Dream Team, led by stars including Nwankwo Kanu, Austin Okocha, Daniel Amokachi, Taribo West, Celestine Babayaro, Garba Lawal and Emmanuel Amuneke, defeated Brazil 4-3 in the semi-finals before coming from behind to beat Argentina 3-2 in the final. The post I’m yet to receive reward for Atlanta ’96 triumph – Bonfrère Jo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Maférinya : deux morts et deux blessés graves dans une collision entre deux motos
items.description: Un grave accident de la circulation s'est produit dans la matinée de ce mardi 4 août 2026, aux environs de 6 heures, à Yoroya, dans le district de Fanyé, relevant de la sous-préfecture de Maferinyah. Selon les informations recueillies sur place, deux motocyclettes sont violemment entrées en collision. La première, en provenance de Fandié, transportait trois personnes, tandis que la seconde, qui venait de Maferinyah, avait deux occupants à son bord. Le bilan provisoire fait état de deux morts sur le coup et de deux blessés graves. Les deux victimes décédées se trouvaient sur la moto en provenance de Maférinyah. D'après les premiers éléments de l'enquête, le conducteur de cette motocyclette aurait tenté de dépasser un véhicule avant de se retrouver face à la moto arrivant en sens inverse. La collision, d'une extrême violence, n'a laissé aucune chance aux deux occupants, qui ont succombé sur les lieux. Les corps des victimes ainsi que les blessés ont été évacués vers le Centre de santé amélioré de Maferinyah, où les survivants sont actuellement pris en charge. Les personnes décédées ont été identifiées comme étant Lamine Soumah , surnommé « Barrage Callé », et M'Mah Ténin Guilavogui , originaire de Foulawa et employée de l'usine Fatala de Yoroyah. Une enquête a été ouverte afin de déterminer les circonstances exactes de ce drame et d'établir les responsabilités.

Garango : Le commissariat de police du secteur 3 inauguré pour renforcer la proximité avec les populations
items.description: À Garango, la sécurité change d'adresse. Un ancien site jadis occupé par les pandores ouvre une nouvelle page de son histoire en devenant le commissariat de police du secteur 3. Bien plus qu'une simple inauguration, cet événement a marqué, ce 1ᵉʳ août 2026, un rapprochement concret entre la Police nationale et les populations, tout en renforçant le dispositif sécuritaire d'une ville en pleine expansion. La cérémonie d'ouverture a réuni le directeur général de la Police nationale, l'inspecteur général de police Thierry Dofizouho Tuina, des autorités administratives, coutumières et régionales, ainsi qu'une foule nombreuse. Le secrétaire général de la région du Nakambé a procédé à la coupure symbolique du ruban, donnant ainsi le top départ des activités de cette nouvelle unité. La sécurité de proximité au cœur de la stratégie Désormais doté de deux commissariats, Garango améliore son maillage sécuritaire afin de rapprocher davantage les services de police des citoyens et de garantir des interventions plus rapides. Cette réalisation s'inscrit dans la mise en œuvre de la vision « Innovation stratégique et opérationnelle pour une sécurité au quotidien (ISOQ) », qui fait de la proximité avec les populations un levier majeur de l'action policière. Face aux agents affectés dans cette nouvelle structure, le directeur général de la Police nationale a insisté sur la qualité de l'accueil réservé aux usagers. Il les a invités à faire preuve d'intégrité, de discipline, de probité et d'exemplarité, tout en incarnant les valeurs de policiers révolutionnaires, progressistes et vertueux au service exclusif des citoyens. Le patron de la Police a également lancé un appel aux populations afin qu'elles s'approprient ce nouveau commissariat, fréquentent ses services et renforcent leur collaboration avec les forces de sécurité. Selon lui, la lutte contre l'insécurité repose autant sur l'engagement des forces de l'ordre que sur la participation active des communautés. Développement local et services aux citoyens Le représentant du gouverneur de la région du Nakambé, tout comme le président de la délégation spéciale de Garango, ont salué cette infrastructure qu'ils considèrent comme un investissement majeur pour la paix, la sécurité et le développement de la commune. En marge de l'inauguration, l'Office national d'identification (ONI) a rapproché ses services des populations en organisant une opération spéciale d'établissement de la carte nationale d'identité de l'AES, permettant à de nombreux citoyens d'effectuer leurs démarches sur place. La cérémonie s'est achevée par la plantation d'un manguier, symbole d'enracinement et d'avenir. Avant de quitter Garango, le directeur général de la Police nationale a effectué une visite au premier commissariat de la ville, où il a salué une initiative citoyenne visant à améliorer le cadre de travail des policiers. Avec l'ouverture du commissariat du secteur 3, la Police nationale franchit une nouvelle étape dans son ambition de bâtir une sécurité de proximité, fondée sur la confiance, la collaboration et une présence renforcée au cœur des communautés. items.title: Yacine Titraoui, le « Verratti algérien », débarque au RC Lens pour la Ligue des champions
items.description: Le milieu international algérien Yacine Titraoui change de club et disputera la Ligue des champions la saison prochaine. Formé au Paradou AC à l’image de Ramy Bensebaini et Youcef Atal, celui qui est surnommé le « Verratti algérien », pour ses qualités qui ressemblent à celles de l’ancien milieu international italien, vient de quitter le club belge de Charleroi pour poser ses valises au RC Lens en Ligue 1 française. Il remplace numériquement Mamadou Sangaré parti à Brentford en Angleterre. Après deux saisons passées à Charleroi où il a montré ses qualités, Titraoui a signé un contrat jusqu’en 2031 avec les Sang et Or. Le RC Lens accueille Yacine Titroui, un joueur avec un « bagage technique haut de gamme » À 23 ans, le milieu axial algérien a un « bagage technique haut de gamme et figurait parmi les meilleurs milieux du championnat belge ces deux dernières saisons », dit de lui Jean-Louis Leca, directeur sportif du Racing Club de Lens qui a terminé la saison à la 2 e place du championnat de France, derrière l’indétrônable PSG. Un dernier message du petit prince algérien. Prenez soin de lui @RCLens #RCSC #NapoleonScore pic.twitter.com/liFKXv1Urc — Royal Charleroi Sporting Club (@SportCharleroi) August 3, 2026 Leca ajoute que Titraoui va apporter au RC Lens sa « faculté à jouer sous pression et constamment vers l’avant ». « Humainement, c’est un garçon simple et travailleur qui nous rejoint », ajoute-il sur le site du club lensois. Pour lui, l’international algérien « incarne l’avenir de l’équipe d’Algérie et celui du Racing ». Un métronome au cœur du jeu Inlassable coureur et chef d'orchestre de l’entrejeu, Yacine Titraoui rejoint le Racing après deux saisons abouties au @SportCharleroi . Récent participant à la @FIFAWorldCup avec l'Algérie , le milieu s'engage jusqu’en 2031. #LesLensois2 — Racing Club de Lens (@RCLens) August 3, 2026 Le RC Lens ne tarit pas d’éloges sur son nouveau milieu axial qu’il présente comme un « inépuisable travailleur ». « ll est aussi le joueur de Jupiler Pro League (championnat de Belgique) qui effectue le plus de courses progressives et de distance en sprint ». En équipe d’Algérie, Yacine Titraoui a été retenu par Vladimir Petkovic pour la Coupe du monde 2026, mais il ne l’a pas fait jouer, lui préférant Nabil Bentaleb, Ramiz Zerrouki ou Hicham Boudaoui. Avec le départ du technicien suisse, le nouveau milieu de terrain du RC Lens devrait avoir sa chance avec les Fennecs. Le futur sélectionneur devrait poursuivre le projet de reconstruction de l’équipe nationale dans lequel Titraoui pourrait avoir sa place. items.title: Congé présidentiel : l’armée réaffirme sa loyauté au président Doumbouya et appelle les Guinéens au calme
items.description: À la suite du communiqué annonçant le départ en congé annuel du président de la République, le chef d'état-major général des armées, le général Ibrahima Sory Bangoura, a lu sur les antennes de la télévision nationale un communiqué pour rassurer les Guinéens sur la continuité de l'État et la stabilité du pays. S'exprimant au nom de l'ensemble des forces de défense et de sécurité, le chef d'état-major a affirmé la « fidélité constante » et la « loyauté indéfectible » des forces armées envers le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, ainsi qu'envers les institutions de la République et le peuple de Guinée. Dans ce communiqué, les forces de défense et de sécurité réitèrent leur engagement à poursuivre le processus de mise en place des institutions de la République, conformément aux dispositions de la Constitution. Elles réaffirment également leur détermination à accompagner les actions de refondation de l'État, estimant que leurs effets sont déjà perceptibles par les populations. Le Général Ibrahima Sory Bangoura assure par ailleurs que les forces de défense et de sécurité demeureront pleinement mobilisées pour garantir la stabilité intérieure et préserver l'intégrité du territoire national, deux conditions qu'il considère comme essentielles à la poursuite de la dynamique de développement engagée dans le pays. « En conséquence, les forces de défense et de sécurité useront de tous les moyens indispensables à l'accomplissement de leurs missions régaliennes », souligne le communiqué. Face aux rumeurs et aux informations circulant sur les réseaux sociaux à l'occasion du congé du chef de l'État, l'état-major général des armées invite les citoyens à ne pas céder à la désinformation et à poursuivre sereinement leurs activités quotidiennes. Le communiqué s'achève par un message de courtoisie adressé au président de la République. Les forces de défense et de sécurité lui souhaitent, ainsi qu'à sa famille, d'agréables congés annuels. Cette sortie du chef d'état-major intervient quelques heures après l'annonce officielle du départ en congé annuel du président Mamadi Doumbouya, dans un contexte marqué par de nombreuses spéculations sur les réseaux sociaux. Par cette déclaration, le haut commandement militaire entend rassurer l'opinion publique sur la continuité des institutions et le maintien de la stabilité du pays.

items.title: The Danger of Trump’s Anti-Communist Rhetoric
items.description: K arl Marx wrote that political actors often borrow the language and symbols of earlier struggles to wage their own battles. So perhaps he would have been unsurprised to hear the Trump administration resurrect the political rhetoric of the Cold War fight against Marxism. President Trump, at Wheeler High School in the Atlanta suburbs earlier this summer, mentioned communism or communist 15 times, starting less than a minute into his hour-plus speech: “Communism is the single greatest threat to our country and its history—including even World War I and World War II, Pearl Harbor, 9/11,” he claimed. “I think it’s the greatest threat that I’ve ever seen to our country.” Last month, Secretary of State Marco Rubio convened political leaders, counterterrorism professionals, and law-enforcement officers from 66 countries for what the State Department billed as an extraordinary gathering aimed at confronting “a transnational threat.” From a podium flanked by world flags, Rubio spoke of the need to combat the far left around the world. “This is a distinctive and unique evil,” he said. “They can call themselves anti-capitalist or anti-imperialist or communist or anarchist or Marxist, but the fundamental character is always the same.” The State Department even has a culprit in mind, last week releasing a 100-page report that characterized Cuba as “posing a unique threat” to American security. Never mind that the island nation of 11 million people lost its chief sponsor with the Soviet Union’s collapse and is so economically strapped that the regime rations electricity and gas. The official line of the U.S. government is that Havana has backed “left-wing terrorism” inside the United States—including “violent BLM militants” and “Antifa terror cells”—and provides a refuge for communism in the Western Hemisphere. “The Cuba that they’re describing, going back to the ’60s and onward, doesn’t exist anymore,” Ted Piccone, a senior foreign-policy adviser for the Clinton administration, told us. “I think they’re just fighting an old ghost in old battles.” From the standpoint of the White House, however, reviving communism as a boogeyman is a way to tie together two very current objectives. On the home front, experts told us that the vilification of Communists could be an attempt to shift the focus away from painful pocketbook issues such as higher gas prices and inflation, and to paint Democrats, and democratic socialists in particular, as anti-American ahead of the midterms. Overseas, fighting Marxism, especially in Latin America, injects principle into the administration’s desire for dominance in the Western Hemisphere, which so far has led to the removal of a leftist dictator in Venezuela and laid the groundwork for the overthrow of the regime in Havana. Tommy Pigott, a State Department spokesperson, said in a statement that the United States will “not ignore the threat posed by a regime 90 miles off our coast intent on undermining the national security of the American people through espionage and the spread of its failed, insidious ideology.” Others see less ideological combat, more exercise of American muscle. “The idea is to get rid of any government in the Western Hemisphere that’s not willing to toe the line,” William LeoGrande, a former dean of American University’s School of Public Affairs, told us. “It started with Venezuela, obviously, and now turned to Cuba.” He added, “If I was Daniel Ortega,” Nicaragua’s autocratic ruler, “I might be a little worried that I’d be next.” [ Read: How to break Cuba ] U.S. voters may regard the revival of the “Reds under the bed” scare as a desperate attempt by an unpopular president to bolster his party’s election chances. Others may see Rubio using an outdated threat as cover to achieve greater American influence. But the push is already having an effect elsewhere, as other Latin American governments paint pro-democracy protesters as Marxists intent on undermining public order to justify crackdowns. T rump and his allies have repeatedly described Democrats as socialists or Communists, regardless of how moderate those Democrats’ positions were. During the 2016 presidential campaign, he referred to Senator Bernie Sanders, a democratic socialist, as just a “socialist.” And the October before the 2018 midterms, Trump wrote in an op-ed in USA Today that the “new Democrats are radical socialists” who want to introduce “open-borders socialism,” and he warned that their economic policies were modeled after the socialist policies of Nicolás Maduro’s Venezuela. He never used the word communism , though, and despite his warnings, Democrats took control of the House. By 2024, Trump was calling his rival for the presidency “Comrade Kamala.” This June, the president again started describing Democratic candidates as “Communist.” Speaking at the Faith & Freedom Coalition’s policy conference, Trump declared : “It’s becoming a communist party. These are not social Democrats; these are hard-core, godless Communists.” A Reuters analysis revealed that Trump invoked the word communism more than 80 times in the two weeks leading up to July 8. The shift followed primary victories by democratic-socialist candidates in New York, California, and Colorado, as well as last year’s sweeping victory by the DSA standard-bearer Zohran Mamdani to become mayor of New York City. Polls currently suggest that the Democrats could win one or both chambers of Congress in November. “The Democrats’ full-blown embrace of socialism and communism is a mortal threat to American liberty,” the White House spokesperson Allison Schuster told us in a statement. “President Trump will never allow America to become a socialist or communist country.” Others in the administration, including Vice President Vance, have echoed Trump’s rhetoric. But no member has been more fervent in his public disdain for Communists than Rubio. His anti-communism is deeply personal. The secretary, the first of Latino descent to serve in the role, is the grandson of Cuban exiles who fled the island as Fidel Castro took power, settling in South Florida, where Rubio grew up. “Marco’s talked about this a lot—growing up in a Cuban American community, you hear the stories: firsthand accounts about repression; about not having basic freedoms; about watching an economy just collapse under that system,” Cesar Conda, Rubio’s former Senate chief of staff, told us. “That stuff shapes you. I think it shaped him, from a really young age.” That hatred of communism became a constant reprise through Rubio’s career in local and state politics in Florida, in the U.S. Senate, and in the Trump administration. “It’s not complicated once you understand where he comes from,” Conda said. “It’s personal, it’s family, it’s ideology, and yeah, there’s a strategic piece to it, too. But the family history—that’s the big one. That’s really where it starts.” Rubio does not hold all Communists to the same standard. Conda recalled that Rubio, while a Senator in 2014, “said he’d never wanted to set foot in Communist China” because of his contempt for communist regimes. His criticism of China’s human-rights record put Rubio on a Chinese sanctions list in 2020—twice. (Rubio’s trip to Beijing with Trump this year was his first.) But Rubio told reporters late last month that China, still home to the world’s largest and most successful Communist Party, would remain a diplomatic partner to the United States. “These are the two most powerful economies in the world, two large militaries, two nuclear powers,” Rubio said. “We have to have a relationship with China, and we want it to be as positive as it possibly can be.” (Imagine President Ronald Reagan saying the same about the Soviets.) Rubio has paid relatively little attention to the other nominally left-wing regime in North Korea. Instead, the administration has depicted Western Europe as a new hotbed of Marxism. The State Department, in recent months, placed four European left-wing groups, including the Germany-based Antifa Ost, on blacklists designed to isolate terrorists, choke off their funding, and protect national security. Advocates of this approach point to an uptick in left-wing political violence. The Trump administration has claimed that left-wing extremists and anarchists are responsible for most terror attacks in Europe, pointing to data from 2022. American officials also emphasize the more than 40 percent increase in violence attributed to left-wing extremism in Germany. Other data tell a different story. In 2025, the European Union member states recorded 11 completed attacks by left-wing extremist groups. But only about a third of completed terror attacks in the EU have been attributed to left-wing actors over the past three years, according to Europol, the EU’s law-enforcement agency. (The highest number of completed attacks was attributed to ethno-nationalist and separatist groups—primarily in France—while jihadist groups were responsible for the largest number of foiled or failed attacks.) In Germany, right-wing extremists continue to account for the largest share of political violence. The German far-right party AfD, which the government deemed an extremist group last year, leads nationwide popularity polls. Farther east, several states that were once Soviet satellites have swung right. Many European countries that used to be under communist control now appear to be on Trump’s side. [ Read: Europe’s far right is turning on Trump ] I n the Trump administration’s ideal world , Cuba might go the way of Venezuela, where military intervention and Maduro’s seizure forced the country into close partnership with the United States. The administration has been piling pressure on Havana to expand its private sector (which would allow greater access for U.S. companies) and to make changes at the top, with the threat of military action if the regime doesn’t yield. The prolonged war with Iran has complicated that campaign, and produced skepticism even among the president’s supporters of the wisdom of foreign intervention. “Some sort of military adventure in Cuba on the heels of a very unpopular war in Iran would be political suicide,” Christopher Hernandez-Roy, the acting director of the Americas Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, told us. “So they have to point to some other things, such as painting Cuba as a geopolitical adversary that’s spreading communism around the world, which is kind of silly.” But it’s a strategy that other leaders have used successfully. Argentinian President Javier Milei, a Trump ally, has described much of his domestic opposition not as fellow citizens with competing ideas but as agents of an ideological enemy. Labor organizers, feminist movements, and left-leaning political groups have all been labeled “Communists” or willing accomplices to a communist project. What the targets believe is almost irrelevant. Once political opponents are cast as part of a larger ideological conspiracy, Milei and his allies can treat them as a threat to democratic life. Milei introduced, then expanded, a sweeping campaign to limit labor strikes, street demonstrations, and other forms of organized dissent. Federal security forces last year moved aggressively to clear picket lines, disperse demonstrations, and prevent protesters from blocking roads after the passage of economic reforms. Protest organizers now face the prospect of criminal investigations, financial penalties, and state surveillance. Trump’s labeling of his political opponents as “Communists” may be a transparent ploy. And Rubio’s portrayal of Havana as a principal exporter of left-wing terror may be impossible to reconcile with the reality of modern-day Cuba. But the administration’s anti-communist vocabulary has nonetheless been embraced by governments far beyond Washington. The result isn’t a new Cold War. It’s the spread of an old political lexicon that can be used to cast political opponents as representatives of a specter that most people thought had long been dispatched.
